story.headline: Coastal water around Kuakata, Bangladesh between 2026-06-18 and 2026-10-16.
story.summary: Over the full season, dark (radar-absorbing) water covered about 173.4 km² on 2026-06-18 and 154.3 km² on 2026-10-16 — a -19.2 km² (-11%) shift. About 97.2 km² (42%) of the analyzed window changed brightness by more than 1.5 dB between the two dates, in 24 clusters.
story.detail: This is derived from calibrated NISAR L-band HV backscatter (gamma-0). Calm water absorbs radar and appears dark; rougher or vegetated surfaces appear brighter. Brightness change alone cannot tell water depth, tide stage, or cause, and NISAR is still provisional, so treat this as situational context, not a flood forecast.

citations: NASA ISRO NISAR L2 GCOV Provisional, Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF), via CMR

limitations: Single-polarization amplitude change; not ground deformation or velocity.
Provisional NISAR calibration; values may shift with reprocessing.
Radar brightness alone cannot confirm water depth, tide stage, or ice thickness.
Not a hazard warning; for situational understanding only.
